newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS HAS NO VOTE ON CEN BANK BOARD.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS HAS NO VOTE ON CEN BANK BOARD.

text.p: The Slovak government on Wednesday said Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik, approved on Tuesday as a participant at central bank board meetings, will have no direct voting rights.
"The advisory right means that the minister has no vote at the board meetings, but his voice can influence the overall vote, of course," ministry spokesman Jozef Mach told Reuters.

"He will not interfere in the board's decisions though, he will only be available at the meetings to let the board know what the country's other (fiscal) side thinks about particular issues being decided upon there," Mach added.

Late on Tuesday, the government said it had agreed to charge Kozlik with participating in central bank board meetings with an advisory right in accordance with the law to enhance the cooperation between the government and the central bank.

"With an interest in better coordination of economic and monetary policies, and closer cooperation between the finance ministry and NBS...the government is to take advantage of a legal posssibility and charge its member with attendance at NBS meetings," a government document obtained by Reuters said.
It did not give any further details.
Central bank officials were not immediately available to comment, but some banking sector analysts said Kozlik previously had the right to attend, though he rarely exercised this option.
